page.title: Nightly Backup Decisions
page.lede: Three invented decisions about a nightly backup, in the working kit's shape, to test the upgrader.
page.note: This page follows the v5 layout.

layers: where the nightly backup is written and how long it is kept.
follow: When should it come back? Blank means the next report.
Anything in particular to show in more detail?
What should I look into first?

tldr: The nightly backup goes to one local disk today
Add an offsite copy, or keep the one disk
cards.context: The nightly backup writes the whole photo library to one local disk in the same room, which the storage review listed as B2 (single backup disk). An offsite copy is a second copy kept in a rented storage bucket.
cards.what: Where the second copy of the nightly backup lives.

finding.what: The backup job writes to one disk only.

open: whether the storage bucket's region matters for the photo library

assume.reason: the disk's age is read from its health report
assumptions: the library stays under two terabytes this year
the upload link is free at night
tripwires: a nightly upload runs past six in the morning

impact.effect: sets how many copies of the backup survive a room fire
impact.wait: the one disk stays the only copy
impact.reach: the photo library and whoever restores it

options.cons: a fire or theft loses every copy
options.plan: Keep the nightly job as it is, writing to the one local disk.
options.effect: The nightly job keeps writing its only copy to the local disk.

options.line: a second copy survives the room
options.pros: a second copy outside the house
options.plan: Add the storage bucket as a second target, uploading after the local copy finishes.
options.effect: Each night the job uploads a second copy to the storage bucket after the local one.
options.reach: The photo library, and the storage bucket's bill.

options.effect: The one disk stays the only copy.

b: Create the storage bucket in the hosting account and paste its name into the backup job's settings page.

background.why: The disk is four years old and its health report shows rising errors.
background.whyask: A monthly bill is the operator's call.

attached.title: Health report
body: Observed: the disk logs rising read errors.
Observed: it is four years old.

attached.title: A restore
body: A restore from the bucket takes about an hour.

tldr: Old nightly backups pile up on the disk
Prune them after thirty days, or keep them all
cards.context: Every nightly backup is kept forever today, so the disk fills in about three months. Pruning deletes the backups older than thirty days.

what.intro: The backups the pruning would delete.

likelihood.text: the disk fills in about three months at today's rate

assume.reason: the disk's free space is read nightly
unknown: whether any old backup is needed for an audit

impact.effect: sets how far back a restore can reach
impact.reach: anyone restoring a photo, and the backup disk
impact.undo: (a) none — a pruned backup cannot be restored

options.plan: Delete each nightly backup once it is thirty days old.
options.effect: Each night the job deletes the backups older than thirty days.
options.reach: Anyone restoring a photo deleted more than thirty days ago.
options.undo: None: a pruned backup cannot be restored.

options.cons: the disk fills in about three months
options.plan: Keep every nightly backup, and buy a bigger disk when this one fills.
options.effect: Every nightly backup stays on the disk until the disk fills and the job stops.
consT: The job stops when the disk fills

background.why: The disk is two thirds full.

attached.title: Free space
attached.body: The disk's free space drops about one percent a night.

tldr: The nightly backup report arrives at midnight
Move it to the morning, or keep it at midnight
cards.context: The backup sends a one-line report when it finishes, today at midnight.
cards.what: When the backup's one-line report is sent.

likelihood.text: the midnight report is read the next morning

assumptions: the report is read once a day
tripwires: a second reader of the report

options.effect: The report keeps arriving at midnight, as soon as the job ends.

options.cons: a failure waits seven hours to be told
options.plan: Hold the report and send it at seven in the morning.
options.effect: The report waits until seven in the morning, then arrives with the day's first mail.

background.why: Raised while the backup job is being changed anyway.
background.whyask: A taste call about the operator's morning.
